verdict: Union Pacific hauled 6% more carloads and turned higher fuel surcharges and core pricing into record revenue of $7.2B and a 16% jump in profit — volume, not just price, did the work.

kpis.label: Operating ratio
kpis.note: costs per $100 of revenue; improved 0.1 pts YoY

segments.name: Bulk
segments.note: Grain, fertilizer, food and coal — farm and energy freight, up 10% YoY.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.note: Chemicals, metals, forest products and energy markets — factory and raw-material freight, up 14% YoY.

segments.name: Premium
segments.note: Intermodal containers and autos — up 21% YoY, with intermodal revenue alone up 27%.

segments.name: Other revenue
segments.note: Non-freight revenue, such as subsidiary and service income — up 21% YoY.

opex.name: Compensation & benefits
opex.note: Pay and benefits for the workforce — up 4% YoY.

opex.name: Fuel
opex.note: Diesel for locomotives — up 69% YoY on higher fuel prices, largely recovered through surcharges.

opex.name: Purchased services & materials
opex.note: Outside services and materials bought in — up 9% YoY.

opex.name: Depreciation
opex.note: Wear and tear on track, locomotives and cars — up 4% YoY.

opex.name: Equipment & other rents
opex.note: Renting cars and equipment from others — down 3% YoY.

opex.name: Other
opex.note: Other operating costs, including casualty and taxes — up 1% YoY.

otherDetail: Other income of $95M, less $312M of interest expense, for a net cost of $217M.
oneTimers: GAAP results include $22M of acquisition-related expense for the planned Norfolk Southern merger — non-deductible for tax and worth $0.04 of EPS. Excluding it, adjusted net income was $2,098M and adjusted EPS was $3.53.
footerNote: Union Pacific does not split out a cost of revenue — every operating expense is a running cost, so gross profit equals revenue in this view.

takeaways.title: Record revenue, real volume
takeaways.text: Revenue hit a record $7.2B, up 15%. Carloads rose 6% and pricing rose too — only part of the jump was fuel surcharges passed through to customers.

takeaways.title: Costs stayed controlled
takeaways.text: The operating ratio — operating costs per $100 of revenue — was 59.1%, a touch better than a year ago, even though fuel costs jumped 69%.

takeaways.title: Profit per share up 16%
takeaways.text: Net income rose 16% to $2.1B and EPS to $3.49. Adjusted EPS was $3.53 after adding back $22M of Norfolk Southern merger costs.
